_comment: Daily reference exchange rates, keyless, so the yen- and won-denominated
trade series can be restated in USD and a currency move can be separated
from a real change in trade.
Primary: the ECB Data Portal's SDMX REST service (data-api.ecb.europa.eu),
no key, no registration. Series EXR/D.<CCY>.EUR.SP00.A is the daily euro
foreign-exchange reference rate: units of <CCY> per 1 EUR, fixed at 14:15
CET on TARGET business days. Requesting D.JPY+KRW+USD.EUR.SP00.A returns
all three in one response, and the cross rate this pipeline stores is
<CCY> per USD = (<CCY> per EUR) / (USD per EUR)
computed per date, so only dates carrying every leg are stored.
Weekends and TARGET holidays have no observation; window averages below
average the business days actually present.
Fallback: frankfurter.app, a keyless wrapper over the same ECB rates. It
is a redistributor, not the primary record (constitution 8.1), so it is
only used when the ECB endpoint fails, and the store records which source
each row came from.
Caveat worth keeping in mind when reading the adjusted series: these are
market reference rates, not the customs conversion rates a customs service
applies when it values a shipment. Japan Customs publishes its own weekly
rate at https://www.customs.go.jp/tetsuduki/kawase/ . For separating a
currency move from a volume move the market rate is the right instrument;
for reproducing a customs valuation to the yen it is not.

quotes.JPY: Japanese yen per USD — restates the MOF trade series
quotes.KRW: Korean won per USD — context only; the KCS series is already USD

_history_start_note: The ECB series reaches back to 1999, and Japan's time-series CSVs reach
back to 1979, so the USD restatement is blank for the early history by
design. 2015 gives a decade of same-window comparables, which is more
than any live watch item needs; widen it with the workflow's fx_backfill
input if a longer run is ever wanted.

_comment: Japan Customs publishes the exchange rates it applies when valuing a
shipment (税関長公示レート). They are fixed weekly, from an average of
an earlier period, and apply to the whole week — so they lag the market
by design. Japan's published trade values in yen embed these rates, not
the market rate, wherever an invoice was in foreign currency.
That makes them the technically correct deflator for Japan's own yen
figures, and the market rate the right instrument for asking what a
flow is worth in dollars today. The pipeline stores both and says which
is which; it does not silently swap one for the other.
The page layout is not known from the build sandbox (customs.go.jp is
unreachable there), so `capture-customs` snapshots the index pages and
any weekly-rate pages they link to into data/fx/raw/pages/, and the
parser is written against those payloads. Candidate index URLs below
are tried in order; whichever answer is saved.
